title: Platform redress can combine worker, consumer, and small-business controls without proving lived recovery
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Grubhub enforcement and refund-administration announcement; affected drivers, diners, and restaurants are distinct groups and not a representative sample
geography: United States federal and Illinois consumer-protection enforcement involving Grubhub platform participants

observations.period: December 31, 2024 court-entered order; payment administration checked September 18, 2026

denominator.unit: affected consumers identified for checks or PayPal payments; group composition not disclosed in the announcement

court_entered_monetary_judgment.unit: US dollars; joint-and-several judgment, with $24.8 million payment and remainder suspended subject to financial representations

court_ordered_payment_to_ftc.unit: US dollars payable within 7 days of order entry; court order also requires a $200,000 Illinois contribution

payment_recipients_identified.unit: affected consumers sent checks or PayPal payments

prospective_account_contestability.value: mechanism for users to dispute blocked accounts

individual_receipt_and_downstream_outcom.value: not observed in the public announcement

payment_acceptance_window.value: check recipients are instructed to cash within 90 days; PayPal recipients are instructed to accept within 30 days
payment_acceptance_window.unit: administrator instruction; not proof of cashing or acceptance

observations.method: Official FTC court-entered order, refund-program page, payment announcement, and active refund-program list; court-ordered payment, administrator-sent payments, and recipient acceptance are retained as separate stages, not as group-specific recovery rates.
observations.uncertainty: The public materials do not separate drivers and diners within the 640,038 payment count, disclose amounts by group, establish individual cashing or PayPal acceptance, identify account correction or restored income, or report continued platform use, alternatives, switching, trust, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Affected Grubhub drivers, diners, and restaurants; eligibility and program denominators are not separately published in the checked announcement.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate payments may resolve some monetary loss while leaving account access, platform visibility, or worker income unchanged; prospective controls may exist formally without being used or enforced consistently.

related_sources.claim: Court-entered order records a $140 million monetary judgment, a $24.8 million payment to the FTC, a $200,000 Illinois contribution, consumer-relief authority, and prospective account, fee, cancellation, pay, and restaurant controls.
FTC lists Grubhub refunds as an active August 2026 refund program and identifies the administrator.

boundary: This record establishes a court-entered multi-sided platform-remedy order, a reported $24.8 million FTC payment obligation, and an administrator-reported 640,038-payment distribution with explicit cashing/acceptance windows. It does not establish group-specific exposure, individual cashing or PayPal acceptance, restored income or access, implementation quality, alternatives, switching, trust, collective action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FTC Grubhub court-entered-order PDF and refund/payment HTML retrieved without retaining repository copies
